name: Falcon
description:
Here is how to read the Falcon config.json. The architecture class is FalconForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 8,192: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 65,024 × 8,192: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 128, so each head sees 64 dimensions (8,192 / 128). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 8192 / 128 = 64. 64 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 8, so this is grouped-query attention (GQA): 128 query heads share 8 key/value groups, so the KV cache is about 16× smaller than full MHA.

num_hidden_layers is 60: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

vocab_size is 65,024. 65,024 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/tiiuae/falcon-40b/blob/main/config.json.
